title: ちゃう / ちゃった: the helper verb しまう
summary: ちゃう is しまう squeezed onto the て-form: "it is done". It can describe regrets, surprises, good news, and even the future.

blocks.text: Textbooks hand you separate meanings of ちゃった ("finished", "by accident", "regret") like the blind men describing an elephant. Look at the elephant instead. **ちゃう** is a contraction of **てしまう**, the helper verb **しまう** (finish, put away) attached to the て-form.

rows: 忘れてしまう → 忘れちゃう
忘れてしまった → 忘れちゃった
〜でしまう (て-form ends in で)
飲んでしまう → 飲んじゃう
踏んでしまった → 踏んじゃった

blocks.text: The word しまった on its own is an exclamation: "That's done it!" And おしまい, the "end" of a fairy tale, is the noun made from しまう.

Imagine English with a helper word **done**: "I done forgot", "I done became a superhero". The sentence says the thing happened, is finished, is a fact, and usually that it was not what anyone expected. The result can be a regret (忘れちゃった), an accident, or great news (なっちゃった). You never need to memorize separate meanings, only the idea "it is done".
It can point to the future

しまう itself is a plain present-tense verb, so ちゃう can look ahead. 今日はどんどん飲んじゃう means "today I'm going to just drink away". 夏休みが終わっちゃう means "the summer vacation will be over before we know it, and nothing can stop it".

blocks.jp: 大事な本を電車に忘れちゃった。
blocks.en: (I) left my important book on the train, oh no.

blocks.jp: 猫のしっぽを踏んじゃった。
まだ七時なのに、もう寝ちゃった。
blocks.en: It is only seven and (he's) already gone to sleep.

blocks.jp: この漫画は読んだら笑っちゃうよ。
blocks.en: (You) will end up laughing if you read this comic.

items: **〜てしまう** becomes **〜ちゃう**; **〜でしまう** becomes **〜じゃう**.
The core idea is "it is done / it happened", often something unexpected.
It can be regret, accident, surprise or good news.
In the present tense it points to the future.

questions.note: ちゃう is てしまう: the helper verb しまう on the て-form.
A て-form ending in で contracts to じゃ.

questions.prompt: ケーキを食べてしまった。
options: ケーキを食べちゃった
ケーキを食べじゃった
ケーキを食べりゃった
ケーキを食べってしまった
questions.note: 食べて + しまった becomes 食べちゃった.
questions.en: I ended up eating the cake.

questions.prompt: ジュースを全部飲ん＿＿った。
questions.note: 飲んで ends in で, so it contracts to じゃ.
なくして ends in て, so it contracts to ちゃ.
questions.en: I lost my key, oh no.

questions.prompt: もうすぐ時間がなくなっちゃうよ。
options: Something will be over before we know it
questions.note: しまう is a present-tense verb, so ちゃう can look ahead.
questions.en: We'll run out of time before we know it!

questions.instruction: True or false: ちゃった always shows regret.
questions.note: It can be regret, an accident, surprise or even good news.

questions.instruction: Which meaning is NOT a use of ちゃった?
questions.note: The core idea is "it is done"; a request is not part of it.

questions.instruction: What is the one idea behind ちゃう?
questions.note: Like the English "I done forgot", it says the thing is finished.

questions.instruction: What is しまった on its own?
questions.note: It is the past form of しまう used as an exclamation.

questions.instruction: What does おしまい, the end of a fairy tale, come from?
questions.note: おしまい is the noun made from しまう: the thing is finished.
で-endings take じゃ: 飲んじゃった.

questions.instruction: Pick the full form of 笑っちゃった
questions.note: ちゃった is てしまった.

questions.instruction: Pick the contraction of 踏んでしまう
questions.note: んで becomes んじゃ.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that holds the contraction of しまう
questions.note: 食べちゃった = 食べてしまった.
questions.en: My little brother ate all the cake.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that is a contracted helper-verb form
questions.note: 遊んで + しまった becomes 遊んじゃった.
questions.en: (We) ended up playing with friends in the rain.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that makes it "it is done"
questions.note: やって + しまった becomes やっちゃった.

questions.prompt: I left my bag at home.
questions.note: The engine, with the contracted helper verb, goes last.
questions.en: (I) left my bag at home, oh no.

questions.prompt: I spilled the coffee on the table.
questions.note: The engine is last; the particle pieces modify it.
questions.en: (I) spilled the coffee on the table.

questions.prompt: I ate all the ice cream.
questions.note: The engine is last; 全部 can come before アイスを or just before the verb.

questions.prompt: I went to sleep too early today.
questions.note: 寝て + しまった becomes 寝ちゃった.
questions.en: (I) went to sleep too early today.

questions.note: やって ends in て, so the contraction is ちゃ.
